summary: Colombier Islands Light, offshore at the entrance to Burnt Islands harbour on Newfoundland's southwest coast: a 1929 fog alarm, with a light added in 1971.

structures.type: square skeleton tower with octagonal upper portion
structures.note: The town says the tower was built in 1929 as a fog alarm, a 36-foot tower with lantern, balcony and concrete base; the Coast Guard list gives 11.3 m.

access.note: The Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse. Lighthouse Friends says the grounds are open and the tower closed. The sources describe no public landing on the island.

events.note: Fog alarm established on Big Colombier Island; the town says the tower was built in 1929 as a fog alarm.
Fog alarm established on Big Colombier Island.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: four sources, all facts drawn from Lighthouse Friends, the Burnt Islands town site, the Coast Guard list and the DFO brochure. No keeper is named by any source read, so the roster is empty. No wreck, storm or rescue at the island was found in the sources read. The record says boat_only: true; no source read says that. Lighthouse Friends says the grounds are open and the tower closed, and that the light can be seen offshore from Burnt Islands. Tower height: record 11.0 m (Wikidata), town 36 ft, Coast Guard list 11.3 m; the story uses the Coast Guard figure. Whether the 1929 fog-alarm tower is the one lit in 1971 is not stated; the town says it was built in 1929 as a fog alarm, and the story follows the town. Wikipedia's Burnt Islands article was read for leads only and is not cited. The 1915 Burnt Island leading lights are separate aids (Coast Guard list, Burnt Islands front and rear range lights) and were not researched as stations. Facts are not verified on the ground. Revised 2026-10-28 by the fact-checker: 'a small island' changed to 'an island' (Lighthouse Friends says 'an island'); 'Coast Guard property' and the landing advice were removed, because no source says the island itself is Coast Guard property; the brochure date is its page-modified date (2019-09-24).
